newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuadorean minister expects end to energy crisis.
newsitem.headline: Ecuadorean minister expects end to energy crisis.

text.p: Ecuador's Energy and Mining Minister Alfredo Adum said Thursday that electricity rationing should become a thing of the past in 1997 thanks to new private generation projects about to come onstream.
"I am confident that this year the energy shortage will be over," Adum said, forecasting Ecuador would generate 447 MW more than in 1997, more than covering its shortfall of 330 MW.

The Andean nation slipped into an energy crisis in 1995 that the government said was the worst in the last 15 years. Energy rationing continues and the government acknowledges it is too strapped for cash to expand state generation capacity.

Ecuador's population of 11.7 million depends for about 70 percent of their energy needs on the Paute hydroelectric plant. But Adum told a news conference three private projects should come onstream in March and five more are expected to become operational in the second half of the year.
The minister forecast that Ecuador should have generation capacity of 1,237 MW next year.

"So if the energy deficit for next year is estimated at 400 MW, an energy surplus will be a reality," he said, adding that he expects increased competition from the private sector to push down tariffs.
